We are advised by the members of the Commission that none of them have received campaign contributions within the last twelve months.
The applicant or any property owner entitled to notice of the hearing may, within fifteen days after the date of the Planning Commission decision, appeal the Planning Commission decision to the City Council (Ord. No. 091-529). A fee is required for filing an appeal with the City Clerkâ€™s office (R05-14).
The Council may, within fifteen days after the date of the decision or on or before the first date following the first Council meeting after the date of the Planning Commission decision, whichever occurs last: 1) Confirm the action of the Planning Commission and grant or deny the application; 2) Set the matter for public hearing and dispose of it in the same manner as on an appeal; or 3) Amend, modify, delete or add any condition of approval which the Council finds is not substantial under the circumstances relative to or affecting the property subject to the application for a development entitlement. Any determination of the Council pursuant to this paragraph shall be conclusive and final.
The Planning Commission reserves the right to modify the order of items shown on the agenda and advises all interested parties to arrive promptly at the commencement of the meeting.

DRAFT

  MINUTES OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES,
  CALIFORNIA

  April 19, 2016

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was
called to order by Chair Thomas at 6:30 p.m. on April 19, 2016, in the City Council Chambers,
340 Palos Verdes Drive West, Palos Verdes Estates, California. The Pledge of Allegiance
followed.

ROLL CALL

Present:  Kao, Evans, Hunter, Welch, Chair Thomas

Also Present: Planning Director Sheri Repp-Loadsman; City Planner Elizabeth Corpuz;
  Assistant City Attorney John Cotti; Julie Cremeans, Minutes Secretary

  *  *  *

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

Camille Feldman (1713 Chelsea Road) spoke about concerns regarding information submitted by
Crown Castle for their wireless telecommunication facilities permit applications, the proposed
locations in residential areas and the design of the proposed poles related to the comprehensive
Crown Castle project.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Chair Thomas, upon confirmation the applicants present understood the suggested conditions of
approval, opened the public hearing, confirmed that there were no interested persons wishing to
voice concerns regarding the application considered for the Consent Calendar, and closed the
public hearing.

  structure located at 3819 Via La Selva. Portion of Lot T, Tract 6887. This project is
  exempt from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3,

  Applicant:  Tomaro Architecture
  2617 N. Sepulveda Blvd., #100
  Manhattan Beach, CA 90266

Planning Commission  1  April 19, 2016
   Owner:  Javier & Jenna Martinez
  4733 Torrance Blvd., #121
  Torrance, CA 90503

MOTION

  Commissioner Kao moved to approve Planning Commission Resolution No. 2016-0876
for 3819 Via La Selva. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Evans and was carried by
unanimous oral vote.

2.  M-1092-16; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for an accessory structure
  exceeding the allowable height at the single family residence located at 3605 Via La
  Selva. Portion of Lot T, Tract 6887. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to
  California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Applicant: Mike Horusicky
  6054 Flambeau Road Rancho
  Palos Verdes, CA 90275

  Owner:  Jamie Yurk

MOTION

  Commissioner Kao moved to approve M-1092-16 for 3605 Via La Selva, exempt from
CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2016-0915 with
standard conditions. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Evans and was carried by
unanimous oral vote.

3.  M-1093-16; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for walls exceeding the
  allowable height within the setback adjacent to the street at the single family residence
  located at 2736 Paseo Del Mar. Lot 10, Block 2230, Tract 7144. This project is exempt
  from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section
  15303.

  Applicant:  Alan McGregor
  16332 Bradbury Lane
  Huntington Beach, CA 92647

  Owner:  Tom & Lori O’Hern

MOTION

  Commissioner Kao moved to approve M-1093-16 for 2736 Paseo Del Mar, exempt from
CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2016-0916 with
standard conditions and the following additional condition: 1) A Minor Modification application
shall be submitted to remove condition of approval #17 of Resolution No. PCR-2006-0165. The
motion was seconded by Commissioner Evans and was carried by unanimous oral vote.

4.  M-1094-16; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for an accessory structure
  exceeding the allowable height at the single family residence located at 2429 Via
  Sonoma. Lot 13, Block 4, Tract 7538 & portion of Lot E, Block 1650, Tract 8652. This

Planning Commission  2  April 19, 2016
   project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14,
  Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Pritzkat & Johnson Architects, Inc.
  306 Vista Del Mar, Suite A
  Redondo Beach, CA 90277

  Owner:  Chris & Shannon Lennertz

MOTION

  Commissioner Kao moved to approve M-1094-16 for 2429 Via Sonoma, exempt from
CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2016-0919 with
standard conditions and the following additional condition: 1) The proposed accessory structure
shall remain outside of the 100-year flood elevation and the existing sewer easement. The
motion was seconded by Commissioner Evans and was carried by majority oral vote with
Commissioner Hunter dissenting.

5.  SC-136/M-1086/G-1548R-16; Consideration of Sports Court, Miscellaneous and revised

  allowable height at the single family residence located at 1412 Via Fernandez. Lot 7,
  Block 6, Tract 8043.

  Applicant:  Scott Martin
  2455 190th St., #A

  Owner:  H J & P E Investment

MOTION

  Commissioner Kao moved to approve SC-136/M-1086/G-1548R-16 for 1412 Via
Fernandez, exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution
PCR-2016-0909 with standard conditions and the following additional condition: 1) Walls and
structures shall not be built within the sewer easement. The motion was seconded by
Commissioner Evans and was carried by unanimous oral vote.

NEW BUSINESS

6.  WT-137-15; Wireless Telecommunication Facilities Application for new equipment
  within the City right-of-way across from 2325 Via Olivera.

  Applicant:  Crown Castle NG West LLC
  300 Spectrum Center Dr., #1200
  Irvine, CA 92618

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Planning Commission  3  April 19, 2016
 Commissioner Kao asked whether the property next door is vacant and the owner has been
notified, and City Planner Corpuz responded that the property to the north and southwest are city
parklands.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Paul O’Boyle (representing Crown Castle at 13269 Deer Canyon Place, San Diego) came
forward and presented the application and pointed out that Crown Castle is providing a service
that is being demanded.

Commissioners Evans and Thomas and Mr. Boyle discussed other towers relative to this one,
alternative locations considered and the number of sites have been approved.

Fred Robertshaw (1725 Chelsea Road) came forward and discussed the April 8th meeting among
city residents and Crown Castle and his concerns that the equipment being installed is not what
was approved and stated that the coverage maps were designed to deceive. Mr. Robertshaw
requested stop lock on all applications, as the Planning Commission cannot make a judgment
without accurate information.

Chair Thomas asked about impacts from equipment in the box differing from what was
approved, and Mr. Robertshaw responded that there is a stronger radiofrequency signal in that
box and added that it is material that it is not what was approved.

Mr. O’Boyle re-approached and advised that the information provided to the City was accurate
and that all plans and radiofrequency information have been updated and provided to the City.

Commissioners Kao and Welch, Chair Thomas and Mr. O’Boyle discussed the LTE coverage
analysis, the height of the pole and a possible updated analysis with a map showing improvement
in coverage.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Jonathan Kramer (technical consultant for the City at 2001 S Barrington Avenue, Los Angeles)
came forward to clarify the coverage maps and the Commission’s time, place and manner
authority for sites in rights-of-way.

Commissioner Hunter asked whether the Commission has any authority over the equipment
inside the box, as long as that equipment does not exceed the mandated threshold of
radiofrequency safety, and Mr. Kramer responded that it is not within the Commission’s
purview. Commissioner Hunter then asked about equipment degrading over time, and Mr.
Kramer responded that these radios don’t have the capacity to come anywhere near the FCC
limit, even with increases.

Commissioner Welch asked about technology changes over time, and Mr. Kramer responded that
any material changes that would alter the output power would have to come back to the
Commission for approval.

Commissioner Kao asked whether a significant gap in coverage issue is beyond the
Commission’s scope, and Mr. Kramer advised that denial would have to be for some lawful
reason, which would not include radiofrequency concerns, and that public or private property is
where the significant gap would become a real question of approval, not right-of-way.

Planning Commission  4  April 19, 2016
 Discussion ensued among the Commissioners, Mr. Kramer and Staff regarding coverage maps,
the possibility waiting to see the net effect of the 10 approved sites and possible overlap between
sites, the City’s response to a group of citizens who have raised concerns, what data can factor
into the Commission’s decision making, the relevance of accurate coverage maps, the number of
sites on the coverage map.

Chair Thomas asked that the Commissioners discuss the merits of this site.

Commissioner Evans commented that he likes the height and incorporating existing street signs
and would like the box moved to within the shadow and shade of the tree in order to be less
intrusive.

Commissioner Hunter expressed concern about approved locations not shown on the map and
commented that this site is part of a system with the Commission having the right to relocate
sites for aesthetic reasons.

Commissioner Kao commented that the proposed site is probably the least intrusive means but
questioned the new SEC requirement for meters to be above ground. Mr. Kramer advised that
there is a wireless telecommunication rig that doesn’t require a meter, but this doesn’t qualify.

Chair Thomas commented that he prefers the 14-foot profile but doesn’t know a better spot for
the cabinet.

Commissioner Kao commented that there’s no harm in continuing the application and
considering Commissioner Hunter and Welch’s comments to the merits of this application.

Planning Director Repp-Loadsman suggested planting native materials as a buffer.

Commissioner Welch commented that the direction he is providing is about having accurate data
presented, which would include all 22 currently approved and proposed sites.

Commissioner Kao asked about the delay in erecting the sites, and Planning Director Repp-
Loadsman advised that Crown Castle will not be getting certain locations up and running until all
approvals are in and that Crown Castle is working to update the coverage maps, but it doesn’t
change the time, place and manner discussions.

Aaron Schneider (representing Crown Castle) approached and agreed to provide the information
asked for. Mr. O’Boyle re-approached and accepted a continuance and noted that other nodes
will be coming in the next two months and that Crown Castle tries to install as the nodes are
approved.

CONTINUED TO THE MAY 17, 2016 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING.

Planning Commission  5  April 19, 2016
 OLD BUSINESS

7.  Planning Commission Resolution PCR-2016-0914 recommending the City Council
  amend Palos Verdes Estates Municipal Code Title 17 (Zoning procedures) and Title 18
  (Zoning regulations) regarding home-sharing, short term, or vacation rentals in residential
  areas.

Planning Director Repp-Loadsman introduced the application, per written material.

Discussion ensued among the Staff and Commissioners regarding prohibited uses.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Elizabeth Kallas (1328 Via Margarita) came forward and discussed preserving the integrity of
the city, the residents favoring an all-out ban, other city bans, and the adverse impacts to the
local hotel industry and property values.

Brian Cork (4008 Via Pavion) came forward in favor of all short-term rentals being banned,
pointing out increased crime rates and strangers into the neighborhood.

Kathryn and Drexel Chapman (608 Via Bodega) came forward to thank the Commission for
addressing this issue. Mr. Chapman commented that the zoning is for single-family residences,
not short-term hotels and advised that every resident he spoke with wants this banned.

Nancy Guenther (1517 Via Castilla) came forward and pointed out that single-family residence
means that one family lives there.

Jim Anastasi (resident of Palos Verdes Estates) came forward and commented that this
application brought neighbors together from all over the Estates, complimented the process and
asked about enforcement.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Kao asked about adding specific language for secondary structures, and Planning
Director Repp-Loadsman advised of the provisions that allow for second units and added that
this ban would apply for the residential property as a whole, whether a second building is
attached or detached.

Commissioner Evans asked about compliance in other cities, and Assistant City Attorney Cotti
advised that the Code provides prosecution in either civil or criminal court with either injunction
or criminal penalties.

Chair Thomas asked about enforcement, and Planning Director Repp-Loadsman advised that the
City will be proactive but also rely on the community to provide notification of problems.

Commissioner Hunter commented that he is ready to approve with the language in both
paragraphs modified for consistency. Commissioners Welch and Kao agreed.

Commissioner Evans thanked the residents for their input, and Chair Thomas added that the
residents’ input shows the value of the process.

Planning Commission  6  April 19, 2016
 MOTION

  Commissioner Hunter moved to recommend approval of Planning Commission
Resolution PCR-2016-0914 to City Council with modifications to the definition of short-term or
vacation rental. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Evans and was carried by
unanimous oral vote.

8.  NC-1539/G-1557/M-1079/M-1080-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility,
  Grading & Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 2101
  Chelsea Road. Lot 6, Block 2100, Tract 7331. This project is exempt from CEQA
  pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Cauthen Design Inc.
  20141 E. Chapman Ave.
  Orange, CA 92869

  Owner:  Kirby & Sally Larson

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Welch asked for an explanation of the decision process for curbing versus
Hollywood berm, and Planning Director Repp-Loadsman advised that the city engineer reviews
the plans and makes recommendations.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Ben Cauthen (architect at 20141 East Chapman Avenue, Orange) and Kirby Larson (applicant at
2101 Chelsea Road) came forward and presented the application.

Commissioner Evans asked whether the plans are what’s proposed for approval, and
Mr. Cauthen confirmed, except for the hip roof. City Planner Corpuz added that the Commission
could add a condition for approval.

Commissioner Welch asked about the hip roof, and Mr. Cauthen provided the details.

Louis Zakin (2112 Chelsea Road) came forward and commented that changes were made to
reduce the impact and agreed with the project.

Sally Larson (applicant at 20141 East Chapman Avenue) came forward and discussed the efforts
to come to agreement with the neighbors, who are now in support of the application.

Clark Kasunich (2108 Chelsea Road) came forward and asked that the chimney on the right be
lowered.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioners Hunter, Welch, Kao and Evans commented that they are ready to approve the
application with a condition of approval.

Commissioner Evans praised the applicant’s interaction with the neighbors to get their support.

Planning Commission  7  April 19, 2016
 Chair Thomas commented that the hip roof solution was exactly what was needed and thanked
the neighbors for coming back to show support of the application.

MOTION

  Commissioner Hunter moved to approve NC-1539/G-1557/M-1079/M-1080-15 for 2101
Chelsea Road, exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning
Resolution PCR-2015-0848 with standard conditions and the following additional conditions: 1)
A license agreement shall be submitted to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the city, its
officers, agents and employees from and against any and all loss, damage, liability, claims,
demands, costs, charges, and expenses, including attorney’s fees, and causes of action of
whatsoever character which the City may incur, sustain or be subjected to on account of loss or
damage to property or loss of use thereof, or for bodily injury to or death of any person arising
out of or in any way connected to the encroachment; 2) A license agreement shall be submitted
to reimburse the City for any costs incurred by the City to repair damage, restore premises, or
satisfy claims incurred by reason of the encroachment; 3) The project creates, adds or replaces
more than 10,000 square feet of impervious surface. Thus, it shall comply with the City’s
municipal NPDES permit and requirements set forth in Municipal Code 13.08.060, Section C; 4)
The existing driveway within the Chelsea Road frontage parkway shall be removed; 5) The
meandering path/house walk within the corner parkway frontage shall be removed; 6) The
existing deteriorating AC dike along the Chelsea Road frontage shall be removed and replaced a
Hollywood Berm and swale transition to the exiting PCC curb return; 7) Payment to the City
treebank shall be required for each street tree approved or required to be removed within the City
right-of-way; and 8) The roof at the southeast corner of the property shall be revised to a hipped
roof. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Welch and was carried by unanimous oral
vote.

9.  NC-1548-15; Consideration of a Neighborhood Compatibility Application for additions
  and remodeling to the single family residence located at 1620 Chelsea Road. Lot 15,
  Block 1272, Tract 7140. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California
  Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  BCI Designs
  2629 Manhattan Ave., #165
  Hermosa Beach, CA 90254

  Owner:  John & Donna Adams

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Bea Ettinger (2629 Manhattan Avenue, Hermosa Beach) came forward and presented the
application.

Chair Thomas asked which proposal the Commission is being asked to approve, and Ms. Ettinger
responded that she would like them to take a look at both proposals.

Chair Thomas advised the applicant that the Commission can only deliberate and approve what
is before it tonight and that a re-proposal would have to be at a different meeting.

Planning Commission  8  April 19, 2016
 John Adams (applicant at 1620 Chelsea Road) came forward and offered to take the proposal off
the table.

Planning Director Repp-Loadsman recommended continuing the application to allow the
applicant to submit the original proposal without re-silhouetting, since it has already been done
once.

Chair Thomas commented that the new roof is a lot more approvable and that the original would
probably get continued or denied.

Mr. Adams confirmed that he would like to go forward with the plans before the Commission
today, and Commissioner Kao advised that the deliberations would be identical to last time if the
silhouetting were returned to what was there before.

Doug Laurin (1616 Chelsea Road) came forward and expressed his support of the application.

Charles John (1625 Chelsea Road) came forward and commented that it is unreasonable to ask
the Adams’ to go through a major roof reconstruction, advised that the houses in the
neighborhood need to be improved, suggested that the objections are inaccurate, and asked the
Commission to reconsider the original plans.

David Trainer (1617 Dalton Road) came forward and advised that he bought his house for the
view and lowering the roofline does help but the trees extend up beyond the roofline, so there is
even more view impact. Mr. Trainer requested a landscape plan to limit the height of the trees.

Eugene Kwon (1621 Dalton Road) came forward and provided a history of tree and ridge height
view impacts. Mr. Kwon discussed his willingness to compromise on the ridge height impact if
the trees are kept trimmed in order to create privacy but not impact views.

Commissioner Welch suggested pursuing the tree impact with the Homes Association.

Mr. Adams re-approached and addressed tree heights.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioners Welch, Hunter, Kao and Evans commented that they are ready to approve as
presented.

Commissioner Kao added that he would like to see the landscaping managed in order to preserve
the privacy of the applicant and preserve the view of the neighbors on Dalton Road.

Commissioner Welch advised that there is a process with the Homes Association associated with
trees and views and that if the Commission puts something prescriptive in the approval it will be
difficult them to enforce. The Homes Association has a separate process and does not enforce
Planning Commission requirements. Neighborhood compatibility deals with structures and
doesn’t give the Commission purview over landscaping.

Chair Thomas commented that this application is approvable and that the applicants have done
what’s reasonable and practicable to mitigate impacts to the neighbor. Chair Thomas added that
the Commission has frequently conditioned foliage to a certain height but recognized that it’s not
enforceable by the City, although it does add something in the record that speaks to the intent.

Planning Commission  9  April 19, 2016
 Planning Director Repp-Loadsman and Chair Thomas discussed Homes Association deeds, the
cost recovery process and how a condition adds an obligation to the City.

Commissioners Kao and Welch discussed using an independent process and independent
mechanism to make a decision.

Commissioner Evans suggested that the residents should get together and figure this out on their
own.

MOTION

  Commissioner Hunter moved to approve NC-1548-15 for 1620 Chelsea Road, exempt
from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2015-0896
with standard conditions. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Evans and was carried by
unanimous oral vote.

10.  NC-1553/G-1566-16; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility & Grading
  Applications for a new single family residence located at 1304 Palos Verdes Drive West.
  Lot 7, Block 6, Tract 8043. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California
  Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Tomaro Architecture
  2617 N. Sepulveda Blvd., #100
  Manhattan Beach, CA 90266

  Owner:  Lydia & Kevin Tracy

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Louis Tomaro (architect at 2617 N. Sepulveda Boulevard, Manhattan Beach) came forward and
presented the application.

Jackie Dojiri (2529 Via Carrillo) came forward and commented that the applicants are improving
the neighborhood.

Simon Salehi (1300 Palos Verdes Drive West) came forward to ask for the applicant to place the
structure somewhere else on the lot.

Dennis Dahlhausen (1324 Palos Verdes Drive West) came forward with concerns about mass
from the street and a neighborhood transition with all massive houses built to the front.

Albro Lundy (1701 Via Arriba) came forward and pointed out changes made in response to the
neighbors and to the Commission’s feedback.

Kevin and Lydia Tracy (owners at 1304 Palos Verdes Drive West) came forward and asked the
Commission to appreciate their responsiveness.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Planning Commission  10  April 19, 2016
 Commissioner Kao discussed the significant changes in size with the previous concerns being
mitigated satisfactorily.

Commissioner Evans also recognized the significant changes and commented on the massive
size of the home.

Commissioner Welch also discussed the significant changes and advised that he is reluctantly
ready to approve the application as presented.

Commissioner Hunter discussed the satisfactory mitigation, the looming effect on the street, the
massive home size and the setback size and also advised that he reluctantly supports the
application.

Chair Thomas discussed the house size and commented that the only material impact is the
degree to which that the house toward the back crowds Mr. Salehi’s property. However, that
crowding is based on the orientation of Mr. Salehi’s house, which exacerbates the problem.
Chair Thomas advised that he is prepared to approve the application as proposed and asked that
the applicants do more to mitigate the crowding.

Commissioner Evans commented that he will go with majority opinion but added that approval
will cause problems down the road in terms of the character of the neighborhood.

MOTION

  Commissioner Hunter moved to approve for 1304 Palos Verdes Drive West, exempt from
CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2016-0913 with
standard conditions and the following additional condition: 1) Payment to the tree bank shall be
submitted for the removal of the trees and one 48-inch box minimum specimen tree shall be
planted in a location reviewed and approved by the City. Alternatively, the owner may plant a
60-inch specimen tree in a location reviewed and approved by the City. The motion was
seconded by Commissioner Evans and was carried by unanimous oral vote.
